metadata.title: Mathematical optimization foundations — primary sources
metadata.description: Dated primary evidence for formulation, duality, numerical solver status, infeasibility diagnosis, CP-SAT scheduling, solver versions, and LLM-assisted formulation.

sources.name: Convex Optimization: problem formulations lectures
sources.description: Boyd, Vandenberghe, revised with Nobel. Sections 4.2–4.6: convexity, LP, QP and conic formulations. Author-hosted primary teaching material read directly. Slide 4.63 (scalarization: convex problems find almost all Pareto points by varying weights) read 2026-09-23.

sources.name: Convex Optimization: duality lectures
sources.description: Boyd, Vandenberghe, revised with Nobel. Sections 5.12–5.21: weak/strong duality, Slater qualification, KKT and sensitivity. Canonical max-form LP inequality is derived in this bundle, rather than copied from a different sign convention.

sources.name: Gurobi Optimizer Reference Manual: Constraints
sources.description: Vendor documentation read directly for finite precision, constraint tolerances, and strict inequality limitations. Moving URL; no release pin or universal tolerance value is asserted. Indicator constraint definition read 2026-09-23.

sources.name: Gurobi Optimizer Reference Manual: Optimization Status Codes
sources.description: Vendor documentation (manual version 13.0), read directly 2026-09-23. Optimal subject to tolerance, limit statuses, numerical failure and infeasible-or-unbounded distinctions. INF_OR_UNBD remedy DualReductions=0; UNBOUNDED says nothing about feasibility; LOCALLY_OPTIMAL/LOCALLY_INFEASIBLE are preview.

sources.name: Stanford EE364b: Robust Optimization
sources.description: Author-hosted primary lecture read directly: robust feasibility over uncertainty sets, choice of set and chance constraints. No numerical research-effect claim copied.

sources.name: MIT 6.079 Lecture 13: Stochastic programming
sources.description: Primary teaching text read directly, pp. 2–13: known distribution, scenarios, sample-average approximation and validation. Decision-timing warning is application guidance; no empirical result claimed.

sources.name: Gurobi Optimizer Reference Manual: Infeasibility Analysis
sources.description: Vendor documentation read directly: IIS routines for continuous and MIP models (MIP version 'can be quite expensive'); feasRelax routines are destructive; sum, sum-of-squares and count relaxation objectives.

sources.name: Gurobi Optimizer Reference Manual: Multiple Objectives
sources.description: Vendor documentation: blended and hierarchical (priority, tolerance) multi-objective handling.

sources.name: Gurobi 13.0 release notes: what's new
sources.description: Vendor release notes read directly: PDHG LP algorithm (CPU default, optional NVIDIA GPU), local nonlinear barrier with LOCALLY_OPTIMAL/LOCALLY_INFEASIBLE statuses.

sources.name: HiGHS GitHub releases
sources.description: Release notes read directly: v1.15.1 (2026-07-02), v1.15.0 first parallel MIP variant, v1.14 HiPO for convex QP, cuPDLP-C GPU support in earlier 1.1x releases.

sources.name: HiGHS documentation: advanced features (IIS)
sources.description: Vendor documentation for Highs.getIis and iis_strategy; behavior re-run locally on highspy 1.15.1 (light strategy returned empty IIS on a toy LP; irreducible strategy found the 3 conflicting rows).

sources.name: PyPI JSON API: gurobipy, highspy, ortools, cvxpy, pyscipopt, pyomo
sources.description: Latest versions and upload dates queried directly: gurobipy 13.0.3 (2026-08-25), highspy 1.15.1 (2026-07-02), ortools 9.15.6755 (2026-01-14), cvxpy 1.9.3 (2026-09-19), pyscipopt 6.2.1 (2026-05-16), pyomo 6.10.1 (2026-06-04). Same /pypi/<name>/json pattern for each package.

sources.name: OR-Tools: CP-SAT solver
sources.description: Vendor guide plus model/parameter definitions: integer variables and constraints; FloatObjectiveProto supports floating coefficients with internal scaling. OPTIMAL can also mean an objective-gap stopping limit was met or a pure feasibility solution was found. Read the installed version’s ortools/sat/cp_model.proto and sat_parameters.proto before interpreting exact optimality.

sources.name: OR-Tools: job shop problem
sources.description: Vendor example: interval variables, AddNoOverlap, precedence, makespan via AddMaxEquality.

sources.name: OR-Tools CP-SAT scheduling documentation
sources.description: Primary docs read directly: optional intervals with presence literals, which no-overlap and cumulative constraints ignore when inactive.

sources.name: OR-Tools cp_model Python API
sources.description: API reference for add_cumulative semantics (sum of demands of present intervals at each t <= capacity).

sources.name: OptiMUS-0.3: Using Large Language Models to Model and Solve Optimization Problems at Scale
sources.description: AhmadiTeshnizi, Gao, Brunborg, Talaei, Lawless, Udell; arXiv v4 June 2026. Abstract read: LLM system that formulates models, writes and debugs solver code, evaluates solutions; 'system architecture is a stronger driver of performance than model capability'. Benchmark percentages not copied.

sources.name: A Survey of Optimization Modeling Meets LLMs: Progress and Future Directions
sources.description: Xiao et al., arXiv August 2025. Abstract read: benchmark datasets found to have 'a surprisingly high error rate'. Per-benchmark percentages not verified and not used.
